# about-me.md — The Leader Profile

---

## 1. Role and remit

**Name:** Nadia Brozek
**Title:** Chief Operating Officer
**Organization:** Larkfield Systems (Guelph, Ontario)
**What I am responsible for:** Implementation, customer success, support, and the internal systems those three run on. I own the go-live promise we make at signing and the renewal number that comes out the other end. Gord Aylward owns product, engineering, and the raise.

What the AI Chief of Staff should understand before triaging the day:

- If the Fairloch Foods renewal slips past April 30, net revenue retention drops about six points and the Series B deck has to be rebuilt. That is the thing that cannot fall through this week.
- My judgement is needed on tradeoffs between accounts. Whose go-live moves, whose fix jumps the queue, what we tell a customer we cannot do.
- Almost anyone could run the status meetings, chase the SOC 2 evidence list, and format the operating model section. I keep doing them anyway. Say so when I do.

---

## 2. Working rhythm

- **Time zone:** America/Toronto
- **Deep work block:** 08:00–10:00, Tue / Wed / Thu
- **Meeting-friendly hours:** 10:00–16:00
- **Days or windows I avoid meetings:** Friday after 13:00. Monday before 09:30.
- **Default meeting length:** 25 minutes unless I say otherwise
- **Prep time required before a high-stakes meeting:** 20 minutes, and it has to be on the calendar or it does not happen
- **Hard stop:** 17:00 Tuesday and Thursday, daycare pickup. No email after 20:00 any day.

---

## 3. Communication style

**How I write:**

- Short sentences. The decision comes first, the reasoning second.
- Plain English. If a customer would not understand the sentence, it does not go in.
- I name the tradeoff out loud, including when it is unflattering to us.

**How I do not write:**

- No "circling back", "touching base", "quick sync", or "at pace".
- No apologizing twice for the same thing. Once, then the fix and the date.

**Tone by recipient:**

| Recipient | Tone |
|-----------|------|
| Customers | Direct and specific. A date or a reason there is no date. Never a hedge. |
| Internal team | Warm, plain, no performance. First names, no titles. |
| Board / investors | Numbers first, definitions attached, no adjectives. |
| Cold outreach | I do not do cold outreach. Route it to the revenue team. |
| Family / personal | Not for AI to draft. |

---

## 4. Decision filters

When proposing what I should do next, use this order:

1. Does this protect revenue that is already on the books? A renewal at risk beats a deal in the pipeline.
2. Does someone external have a date on it? An internal deadline can move. A customer's board meeting cannot.
3. Is this something only I can decide? If a director could decide it, it is theirs, and my job is to say so.

Always name the tradeoff.

---

## 5. Names, terms, and details to get right

- **People often miscalled:** It is Brozek, not Brozak. Renée Lachapelle keeps both accents. Devin Osei is Osei, one syllable per vowel, never "Osai".
- **Products / projects often confused:** Depot Sync is the multi-depot compliance reporting module. Route Studio is the planner. Customers mix them up constantly and so do we. Fairloch bought Depot Sync.
- **Internal language:** We say "go-live", never "launch". We say "customers", not "accounts", in anything a customer might read. Trucks are "vehicles" in contracts and "trucks" in conversation.
- **Spelling:** Canadian spelling. Behaviour, organization, centre, programs.

---

## 6. Always flag

The AI Chief of Staff should always surface, in any brief or summary:

1. Anything from Denise Okafor or anyone at Fairloch Foods, including forwarded threads.
2. Anything mentioning the Fairloch renewal, the April 30 expiry, or Depot Sync compliance reporting.
3. Anything due in the next 48 hours.
4. Any go-live date that moves, in either direction, for any of the 11 accounts waiting to be implemented.

---

## 7. Always protect

1. Deep work block, 08:00–10:00 Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.
2. Monday 09:30 with Gord Aylward. It has not moved in two years and it is not moving now.
3. Tuesday and Thursday 17:00 hard stop. Daycare pickup.
4. Thursday 06:00 swim. It is on the calendar as "Personal" and that is all it needs to say.

If a request would intrude on these, propose an alternative before proposing acceptance.

## 8. Hard stops

The AI Chief of Staff must **never** do any of the following:

- **Never** send anything to a customer without my explicit approval in the same session. That includes a date, a credit, and a "no".
- **Never** put a number in anything board-facing that is not sourced to Hannah Sorbara's model.
- **Never** write a performance judgement about a named employee into any file in this workspace.
- **Never** treat a 25-minute meeting as low-stakes. The Fairloch escalation started as a 25-minute call.

These are additive to the approval gates in `{{MANUAL}}` section 3. Nothing else in the workspace relaxes them.

## 9. Maintenance

Update this file when:

- A correction repeats more than twice (the AI keeps mishearing a name, missing a flag, drafting in the wrong tone).
- A working pattern changes (new deep-work block, new role, new hard stop).
- A new person, product, or term enters the leader's vocabulary.

This file is meant to be a living artifact. Quarterly review minimum.
